report.summary: Reviewed drift.py chunk 3 (lines 561-~700): scan, Acceptance, parse_acceptances, DriftItem, DriftReport. Claims largely kept; some uncheckable due to cross-module references.
risks: line 0 | medium | scan() docstring claims 'Pure: no writes, no clock, no network' but it imports reach and switches modules and calls repo_state which may read git HEAD; actual side effects depend on those modules. | Inspect reach.analyse, switches.analyse, repo_state for filesystem/network access.

line 0 | low | 'unparsable' set merges reach and switch unparsable entries; format of switch_report.unparsable is not pinned, so parsing by ':' might mis-handle future formats. | Check switches module for unparsable entry format.

line 0 | medium | Acceptance.expired() returns True on ValueError (malformed date), which is fail-open; docstring says 'Fail closed' for parse_acceptances, but expired() is a separate method. | Verify intended semantics for malformed dates in expiration.
line 0 | low | parse_acceptances returns [] for non-list input silently; could mask malformed configuration. | Check callers to see if silent empty list is desired.

line 0 | medium | DriftReport.blocking property filters items where blocking is True; but the definition of blocking depends on NON_BLOCKING_KINDS and accepted flag. The docstring in DriftReport says 'Reported, never blocking' for freshness, but the property does not consider freshness. | Verify intended blocking semantics for freshness.

handoff.purpose: Contains scan(), Acceptance, parse_acceptances, DriftItem, DriftReport dataclasses.

symbols.name: scan
symbols.note: Builds ScanResult from reach/switch reports, DocIndex, and repo_state. Pure in the sense of no writes/network, but may read git HEAD via repo_state.

symbols.name: Acceptance
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with item, why, since, until, who, problem. Properties: valid, expired, as_dict.

symbols.name: Acceptance.valid
symbols.note: Returns True if problem is empty.

symbols.name: Acceptance.expired
symbols.note: Returns True if today > until, or True on ValueError (malformed date).

symbols.name: Acceptance.as_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict with item, why, since, until, and optionally who.

symbols.name: parse_acceptances
symbols.note: Parses raw list into Acceptance objects, marking problems. Returns sorted list.

symbols.name: DriftItem
symbols.note: Dataclass with kind, key, subject, detail, remedy, accepted, note. Property: blocking; method: as_dict.

symbols.name: DriftItem.blocking
symbols.note: Returns False if kind in NON_BLOCKING_KINDS, else not accepted.

symbols.name: DriftReport
symbols.note: Dataclass with ok, first_run, snapshot_path, items, state, snapshot, wrote_snapshot, freshness. Property: blocking.

symbols.name: DriftReport.blocking
symbols.note: Returns list of items where i.blocking is True.

claims.text: Pure: no writes, no clock, no network.
claims.why: The function itself does not write/clock/network, but it calls repo_state which may read git HEAD; side effects of imported modules are not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: reach_report and switch_report may be injected by a caller that already built them
claims.why: The function checks if reach_report is None and switch_report is None, otherwise uses the provided ones.

claims.text: index is only forwarded to reach for its structural cross-check.
claims.why: index is passed to reach_mod.analyse(root, index=index) when reach_report is None.

claims.text: The state also records WHICH TREE it was derived from (:func:repo_state).
TEST ONLY is a property of an UNREACHED module, not of an island specifically.
claims.why: test_only is derived from unreached_facts (classification in UNREACHED_CLASSES) and m.tested_by, not limited to islands.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature.
claims.why: The code skips switches where sw.kind == 'secret'.

claims.text: A module the scanner could not parse contributes nothing to either engine's answer, which makes it a hole in the map that used to be filled by a bare continue. It is a finding, not a shrug.
claims.why: unparsable set is collected and included in state, counts, and sites.

claims.text: Fail closed: anything we cannot fully validate is kept, marked with a problem, and suppresses nothing.
claims.why: Every entry produces an Acceptance, even malformed ones, with problem field set.

claims.text: A typo in an acceptance must never be the thing that makes an island invisible.
claims.why: Items with problems are still included in the output list; they do not suppress anything.

claims.text: today binds the horizon to the CALENDAR.
claims.why: The code checks d_since > today and d_until - d_since > timedelta(days=MAX_HORIZON_DAYS) when today is provided.

claims.text: Without it the only rule is until - since <= MAX_HORIZON_DAYS, which a pair of dates in 2999 satisfies while suppressing forever; the cap measured the acceptance against itself and nothing measured it against now.
claims.why: The horizon check is only applied when both dates parse; if today is None, the d_since > today check is skipped, but the horizon check still applies. However the claim says 'only rule' without today, but the code also checks 'until' before 'since' and date format, so 'only' is slightly overstated. The core point about the cap being relative to itself is true.

claims.text: Omitting today keeps the date-shape and horizon checks and skips only that one, so a caller that genuinely has no clock (--accept validating a candidate before writing it) still gets everything else.
claims.why: The date format and horizon checks are independent of today; only the 'since in future' check is skipped when today is None.

claims.text: Which tree the SNAPSHOT was generated against, versus the one just scanned. Reported, never blocking: a baseline taken one commit ago is not a defect, and a gate that goes red on every commit is a gate people switch off.
claims.why: The field is included in the dataclass with a comment stating it is reported, never blocking. The blocking property does not consider freshness.

claims.text: The consumers that RANK WORK out of these lists are the ones that must fail closed on it -- see :func:snapshot_freshness.
claims.why: snapshot_freshness is defined elsewhere in the file; this chunk cannot verify its behavior.

observations.what: scan() claims to be pure but calls repo_state which may invoke git commands (reads HEAD). The actual side effects depend on repo_state implementation not in this chunk.
parse_acceptances returns [] for non-list input silently, which could mask malformed configuration.
Acceptance.expired() returns True on ValueError (malformed date), which is fail-open. The docstring for parse_acceptances says 'fail closed', but that refers to parsing, not expiration.

The 'unparsable' set merges entries from reach_report.unparsable and switch_report.unparsable by splitting on ':' and taking the first part. The format of switch_report.unparsable is not pinned in this chunk, so a format change could silently misparse.

DriftReport.blocking property returns items where i.blocking is True, but the definition of blocking depends on NON_BLOCKING_KINDS and accepted flag. The docstring says freshness is never blocking, but the property does not explicitly exclude freshness-related items; it relies on item kind.
